title: A pre-rasterised PNG vs a SIMPLE SVG, on tiles rebuilt every frame
variable: PNG texture vs a 4-shape SVG source, same picture, tiles destroyed and recreated
claim: The complexity half of the SVG-vs-PNG question. png-vs-svg-churn-complex uses a 900-path sprite sized like the production flag assets that prompted these cases; this case is identical in every other respect but draws a 4-shape sprite, the size of a UI icon. The pair separates two very different pieces of advice: if both are expensive, the cost is in the SVG pipeline itself and vector assets should not be used for anything that churns. If only the complex one is expensive, the cost tracks path count, simple vector icons are fine, and the rule to write is about asset complexity rather than about SVG.
result: Confirmed on the hypothesized axis (Styles), and the answer is that complexity is a MULTIPLIER, not the cause. A 4-shape SVG - about as simple as a vector asset gets - still costs 4.16x Styles at 30, 3.16x at 100 and 4.20x at 300 against the PNG rasterised from it, with Paint at 4.75x/17.86x/55.04x and RecordRendering at 40.80x/60.76x/87.29x. Absolute numbers at 300: 6.88ms Styles and 0.34ms Paint for the PNG against 28.88ms and 18.77ms for the SVG. Set beside png-vs-svg-churn-complex's 462x at the same count, path count multiplies the penalty by roughly 100x - but it does not create it. The rule this pair supports is therefore 'do not let SVGs churn', NOT 'keep churning SVGs simple': even a trivial vector pays 3-4x on every element creation. Unlike the complex case this row held a healthy frame rate (29-32fps, 119-161 frames per trace in both variants), which makes it the more precisely measured of the two. LIMITS: one shared texture URL; cohtml 3.1.2.1 while the rest of results.md is 3.2.0.2.
notes: Applicability gate: ADAPTED, identically to png-vs-svg-churn-complex - the rebuild runs every frame rather than at pagination rate, because the lab reports steady-state medians and a low-duty-cycle rebuild would fall outside them and return a false null (AUTHORING.md rule 6, the duty-cycle trap). Read the ratio as the cost per rebuild, not as the cost of a pagination UI. SVG as a url() source is not in the ../gameface-unsupported-features inventory either way, and it is the one thing that MUST be confirmed in the Player before a row from this case is trusted: if cohtml silently drops an SVG background, B renders empty tiles and the lab reports SVG as dramatically FASTER - a confident, inverted result. VERIFIED on Player 3.1.2.1: B.html renders 30 tiles at 88x64 with getComputedStyle reporting url(sprite.svg), and a screenshot shows the sprite drawn and matching A.html's. Re-check this on any engine version this case is re-run against. Rule 1: one variable, the asset format. Rule 2: identical DOM at the end of every frame. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte - and byte-identical to the script in png-vs-svg-churn-complex, so the two cases differ only in the sprite the generator wrote into each directory. Rule 4 EXCEPTION: the two variants load different assets - that IS the variable. tools/make-svg-cases.js rasterises sprite.png from sprite.svg itself. NOTE on cross-case comparison: this case and png-vs-svg-churn-complex draw DIFFERENT pictures, so only their B/A ratios are comparable, never their absolute numbers. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: the churn replaces the root-nudge driver and starts at load. Rule 7: no randomness at runtime; the sprite generator is seeded. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is Styles, as in the complex case. LIMIT: every tile shares one texture URL, the most favourable case for any raster cache the engine keeps.
